title: SmoothPL.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The admissible class permits nonconvex objectives: global smoothness and the PL inequality are required, without convexity.

problem_class.label: pl
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization with an attained global minimum and global PL inequality 2μ(f(x)−f(xstar)) ≤ ‖∇f(x)‖². Parameters satisfy 0<μ≤L, Δ≥0, ε>0, and f(x0)−f(xstar)≤Δ.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Every query x returns the exact gradient of f at x for every call index and oracle seed. No function-value information or oracle error is supplied.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothPL.lean: PLGradient.spec.Query, Reply, and admissible, requiring HasGradientAt f (oracle.answer k x seed) x.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is an arbitrary real Hilbert space, potentially infinite dimensional. The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz. E, L, and x0 are public; μ, Δ, and ε are hidden from the algorithm constructor, although they determine the fixed execution budget.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothAndConvex.lean: Gradient.Public; LongTails/Setups/SmoothPL.lean: PLGradient.Params, spec.publicInput, and admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm and budget.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a point in E satisfying f(output)−f(xstar)≤ε for some global minimizer xstar. No gradient-norm or distance requirement is imposed.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap requirement holds almost surely under the output probability law, which in Convergence uses the product of algorithm and oracle seed laws.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Smooth unconstrained PL minimization with exact gradients, an initial objective-gap bound, and objective-gap accuracy is an established standard formulation, including its Hilbert-space version.

descriptionHtml:
Smooth Polyak–Łojasiewicz Minimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, and f satisfies the Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality with parameter 0<μ≤L. A global minimizer x⋆∈E exists, and a given starting point x0∈E satisfies f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ, where Δ≥0. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x. For ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives only E, L, and x0; the parameters μ, Δ, and ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere on E, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈E.

Assumption 2 (Polyak–Łojasiewicz inequality and initial gap). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ,2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤∥∇f(x)∥2for every x∈E.

Queries may be made at any point of E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. The minimizer is fixed independently of the algorithm’s randomness; any global minimizer gives the same objective value.

theorems.referencesHtml: • B. T. Polyak. Gradient methods for minimizing functionals. 1963 (Russian original). Complexity: O(⌈(L/μ)log⁡(Δ/ε)⌉) exact-gradient oracle calls for 0<ε<Δ, and zero calls when Δ≤ε; fixed-step gradient descent gives f(xK)−f∗≤ε with a fixed budget.
theorems.formulaHtml: ⌈Lμ⋅log⁡(1+Δε)⌉+

comparisonHtml:
On a real Hilbert space, f has an L-Lipschitz gradient and a global minimizer x⋆, with f(x0)−f(x⋆)≤Δ and 2μ(f(x)−f(x⋆))≤∥∇f(x)∥2 for all x. Here 0<μ≤L, Δ≥0, and ε>0; convexity is not required. The oracle returns exact gradients. Target: f(xK)−f(x⋆)≤ε deterministically. The setup does not restrict the algorithm; (1) constructs GD with step 1/L.

Smooth PL optimization: SmoothPL.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) GdPL (Ours) (review) O(1+Lμlog⁡(1+Δε)) gradient calls
(2) GD (Karimi et al. 2016, Theorem 1, arXiv v4) O(1+Lμlog+⁡Δε) gradient calls; stated on Rd (1): Matches known rate for ε≤Δ/2. Lean formalization on Hilbert spaces; the dimension-independent classical proof extends unchanged. (1): Explicit stopping budget needs a known Δ; (2) states convergence in the actual initial gap.
(3) Lower bound (Yue et al. 2023, Theorems 2–3, arXiv v2) Ω(Lμlog⁡Δε) gradient calls; deterministic first-order methods, L/μ>C, 0<ε≤Δ/16 (1): Matches (3) up to constants in this regime. A problem-class lower bound, not a competing algorithm; randomized methods are not covered.

Abbr: GD: gradient descent; PL: Polyak–Łojasiewicz; L: gradient Lipschitz constant; μ: PL constant; Δ: initial objective-gap bound; ε: target gap; K: gradient-call count; log+⁡t=max{0,log⁡t} for t>0, with log+⁡0=0; C: universal positive constant.

import LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex

namespace LongTails.Setups.SmoothPL

open OracleTemplate

structure Params extends LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex.Public where
  μ : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := LongTails.Setups.SmoothAndConvex.Public
  Instance p := p.E → ℝ
  Query p := p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.μ ∧ p.μ ≤ p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f oracle :=
    (∀ k seed x, HasGradientAt f (oracle.answer k (0, x) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ f p.x0 - f xstar ≤ p.Δ ∧
      ∀ x, 2 * p.μ * (f x - f xstar) ≤ ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2)
  successful p f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ p.ε

end LongTails.Setups.SmoothPL
